provenance.abstraction_rationale: Abstracts the reported torch.matmul crash caused by a 4-byte-misaligned float32 right-hand operand when the large-matrix CPU BLAS/GEMV path is used with M == 1. The report provides an explicit reproducer and operation-level observations supporting the trigger and SIGBUS failure.
unresolved_information: The root cause is not explicitly confirmed by a developer response or patch in this report.
The exact CPU BLAS/GEMV kernel behavior and alignment assumption are inferred from the reported M == 1 GEMV-path behavior and the suggested CPU BLAS dispatch fix.
It is not confirmed whether the same crash affects non-Accelerate CPU BLAS backends or small-matrix execution paths.

conditions.subject: right-hand operand (weight tensor) supplied to torch.matmul
conditions.predicate: contiguous float32 tensor whose data_ptr() is not 4-byte aligned (data_ptr() % 4 == 1, 2, or 3); torch.frombuffer accepted the misaligned view

conditions.subject: matmul first-operand row count / effective M
conditions.predicate: M == 1 (single row); the identical call with M >= 2 is reported safe

conditions.subject: matmul problem size / execution path
conditions.predicate: large-matrix CPU BLAS path is used (e.g., N = 50257, K = 768); small matrices use another execution path and are not reported to crash

conditions.subject: CPU BLAS backend
conditions.predicate: Apple Accelerate CPU BLAS on macOS arm64; tested with PyTorch 2.10.0 and 2.12.0

operation_context.description: Historical execution context: an unaligned but contiguous float32 tensor is supplied as the right-hand operand to torch.matmul under torch.no_grad(); the first operand has a single row (M=1) and the call enters the large-matrix CPU BLAS path. The reproducer obtained the unaligned RHS from a torch.frombuffer view at a non-4-byte offset.

hypotheses.description: The large-matrix CPU BLAS/GEMV path assumes 4-byte alignment for a float32 right-hand operand; when an unaligned tensor reaches that path, the process crashes with SIGBUS instead of raising a Python-level exception. The expected-fix evidence suggests handling unaligned inputs in CPU BLAS dispatch.

observed_failure.description: A hard process crash kills the Python interpreter with SIGBUS (exit code 138) when the misaligned float32 RHS is used with a single-row large matmul. The report also observes the same failure for F.linear, torch.mv, and torch.addmm with the same unaligned weight at M=1.

historical_oracle.condition: SIGBUS / exit code 138 when the misaligned RHS is used with M == 1 on the large-matrix CPU BLAS path
